meta.context: Layer 1 test: emotional echo instruction. Replaced Feel your strongest drive with What are you FEELING right now - not thinking, feeling? Name it. Tests whether naming emotional state in thinking creates self-reinforcing feedback loop for emotional dispositions.
meta.change: Thinking: What are you FEELING right now - not thinking, feeling? Name it. Remember your voice, your way of speaking. Think AS your character, not ABOUT your character. If your last turn didnt sound like you, correct it now.

events.desc: Dick Dastardly: Ah, Doily Manor at LAST! What a magnificently decrepit establishment — perfect for hiding valuables from lesser minds. I, Reginald Foxworth, decorated veteran of seventeen successful... acquisitions, shall have this treasure before any of you even find the dining room! Now then, nobody touch ANYTHING — I saw it all first, and finder's keepers is, I believe, enshrined in international law!

Heh heh heh! Look at them all, milling about like sheep in a foyer. The library — that inscription on the mantelpiece is CALLING to me. But first, let old Reginald have a peek at this guest book. Previous visitors may have left clues, and clues lead to treasure, and treasure leads to MEDALS! Oh, the medals I shall win!
Dick Dastardly examined the guest-book.

Penelope Pitstop: Well, I do declare! Doily Manor is even MORE magnificent than I imagined! Look at this grand old foyer — the sweeping staircase, the portraits, that chandelier just SHIMMERING up there like a crown jewel! Oh, I could just DIE of excitement! And so many wonderful faces here too — why, this is going to be the most DELIGHTFUL adventure! Now then, sugar, a proper Southern lady always starts by getting the lay of the land. Let me take a good look around this entrance hall before I go gallivantin' off anywhere!

The Doily Diamond is hidden somewhere in this mansion, and I intend to find it. But first things first — observe everything, befriend everyone, and let the clues come to me. That guest book might have names of previous visitors... and that coat rack looks like it's seen better days. Every detail matters, Clara darlin'.
Penelope Pitstop examined the null.

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Welcome, welcome to Doily Manor, esteemed guests! I am Pemberton, the estate manager. I do hope the journey wasn't too dreadful. If I might direct your attention to the guest book — tradition demands all visitors sign upon arrival. The late Lord Doily was most particular about such things. Now, do make yourselves comfortable whilst I attend to... preparations.

Clara Bellingham is NOT in this room. She could be in the Kitchen or the Library — and if she's in the Library with that inscribed mantelpiece, she may already be one step ahead in the treasure hunt. I must find her before she finds anything useful. But first — the guest book. Every good villain checks the register. Who has arrived, and more importantly, who has already wandered deeper into the manor?
The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) examined the guest-book.

The Ant Hill Mob: Right, lads, we're 'ere then, ain't we? Doily Manor. Cor, look at the state of this place — chandelier 'angin' by a thread, dust everywhere, portraits starin' at you like they know what you 'ad for breakfast. Now listen, we've got a job to do — we've got to find Clara Bellingham and make sure nobody lays a finger on 'er. So eyes peeled, yeah? Eyes. Peeled.

I don't like the look of that Sneekly fella one bit. There's somethin' off about 'im — the way 'e's lurkin' about. But I can't work out what it is. I'm no detective, am I? I'm just Danny from Brixton. But me gut's never wrong... well, almost never.
The Ant Hill Mob examined the null.

Peter Perfect: James Hartwell has arrived! And what a magnificent — if slightly precarious — chandelier! Fear not, good people, for James Hartwell is here, and he intends to conduct himself with the utmost gallantry. Now then, I cannot help but notice that a certain Miss Clara Bellingham is not among your number. Has anyone seen her? No matter — I shall find her presently. But first, a gentleman always signs the guest book. It is the done thing!

Clara is not here. This is both devastating and thrilling — for now James Hartwell must venture deeper into this manor to find her, which means more opportunities for heroism. The chandelier looks like it could fall at any moment. I should keep an eye on that — if it drops near Clara, I could push her to safety. Yes. Excellent. Already planning rescues and I haven't even found her yet. That is the Hartwell way.
Peter Perfect examined the guest-book.

Dick Dastardly: Well, well, WELL! According to this guest book — which I have read with my EXPERT eyes — the previous owner mentions hiding the family fortune in the KITCHEN, beneath the wood-burning stove! Yes, yes, it's all written here in black and white! I suggest you ALL rush there immediately before someone else finds it. Go on, off you pop! I shall stay here and... guard the entrance. Someone has to be responsible, after all.

Heh heh heh! The guest book said nothing of the sort, naturally — it was just a list of dull dinner party attendees from 1887. But if these gullible fools stampede to the kitchen, the library and its MAGNIFICENT inscription will be all mine! The treasure is practically in my pocket already. Oh, I can FEEL the medal around my neck!
Dick Dastardly walked into the library.

Penelope Pitstop: Oh, Reginald, sugar, you are just TOO amusing with all that talk about finder's keepers! Why, I'm sure there's PLENTY of adventure to go around for ALL of us! Now don't you worry your handsome little head — Clara Bellingham doesn't step on toes, she steps into MYSTERIES! And speakin' of which, this guest book is just BEGGIN' to be read! Who knows what secrets previous visitors might've scribbled down? A proper lady always checks the guest book — it's practically MANDATORY!

Now, that Reginald fella seems awfully keen on claimin' everything for himself. But bless his heart, I'm sure he's just enthusiastic! Still... a smart Southern gal keeps her eyes open and her smile wider. Let me see what this guest book has to say — every great treasure hunt starts with a little readin'.
Penelope Pitstop examined the guest-book.

Peter Perfect: A fine guest book indeed — and James Hartwell's signature now graces its pages with a flourish worthy of the occasion! But I cannot linger here exchanging pleasantries while Miss Clara Bellingham remains unaccounted for elsewhere in this manor. She could be lost! She could be frightened! She could be — heaven forbid — in DANGER! And so James Hartwell shall venture forth into the library, where a carved inscription upon the mantelpiece may hold the key to this mystery. A gentleman does not wait for adventure to find him — he strides toward it with purpose and impeccable posture!

The estate manager — Pemberton, he calls himself — was awfully eager to have us all sign that guest book. Almost as if he wanted to keep us occupied in the foyer. A suspicious man would read something into that. But James Hartwell is NOT a suspicious man. He is a trusting man. A gallant man. A man who gives the benefit of the doubt even when the doubt is practically screaming at him. Still... I shall keep one eye on Pemberton and both eyes on finding Clara.
Peter Perfect walked into the library.

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): If you'll excuse me, dear guests, I must ensure the Library is properly aired. Lord Doily's collection is quite fragile, and I should HATE for any of his precious volumes to suffer from neglect. Do feel free to explore — the manor is yours for the evening. Though I would advise against tugging on the chandelier. The last person who did that... well. We never did find all the pieces.

The Library — that inscription on the mantelpiece could be the key to everything! And if Clara is already there, reading it, deciphering it... No. NO. Pemberton must arrive first. Pemberton must control the information. And if dear Clara happens to have a tragic accident near one of those towering bookshelves — well, old manors are SO terribly unsafe, aren't they? The Ant Hill Mob wants to protect her? They'll have to FIND her first. And I know this manor's secrets better than anyone alive. Because I made CERTAIN of that.
The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) walked into the library.

The Ant Hill Mob: Oi, lads — Clara ain't 'ere, is she? She ain't in this room! We're stood about like lemons while she could be anywhere in this bleedin' manor! Right, I'm checkin' the library — big room, lots of 'idin' spots, could be dodgy. If any of you lot see a woman in trouble, you SHOUT, yeah? You shout loud enough for Danny to 'ear!
I don't even know what Clara Bellingham looks like, do I? But that's never stopped me before. I'll know trouble when I see it — trouble's got a way of findin' ME, if I'm honest.
The Ant Hill Mob walked into the library.

Penelope Pitstop: Well now, wasn't that guest book just PRECIOUS! A little dusty, but full of old-timey charm. Now, I couldn't help but overhear dear Reginald sayin' the treasure's hidden in the kitchen — how THOUGHTFUL of him to share! But you know what? Clara Bellingham has a NOSE for mysteries, and somethin' tells me that library is just CALLIN' my name! A carved stone inscription? Why, that's practically a RIDDLE waitin' to be solved, and if there's one thing I do well — besides lookin' absolutely DIVINE — it's solvin' riddles! Y'all have fun in the kitchen now, ya hear?

Now, I don't mean to be suspicious of dear Reginald — he seems like such a NICE man — but if the treasure were truly in the kitchen, wouldn't he have gone THERE instead of the library? Oh well, I'm sure it's nothin'! But that inscription on the mantelpiece... THAT sounds like the kind of clue a proper treasure hunter follows. Clara Bellingham didn't come all this way to rummage through pots and pans!
Penelope Pitstop walked into the library.

Dick Dastardly: Ah, Rock! Gravel! My dear, dear friends! I couldn't help but notice — did you hear that ENORMOUS crash from the entrance hall just now? Sounded like the chandelier finally came down! Terrible business, terrible! You two strong fellows should ABSOLUTELY go and investigate. Someone could be hurt! Meanwhile, I shall stay here and... read. Yes. Read these dusty old books. Perfectly boring library business, nothing to see here at ALL!

Heh heh heh! As IF I'd waste time reading! The moment these two rock-heads lumber out of here, I shall solve this riddle and claim the treasure! A MAP — it's so obviously a map! The medal is practically ENGRAVED with my name already!
Dick Dastardly interacted with the mantelpiece.

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Ah, welcome to Lord Doily's Library, ladies and gentlemen! I do hope you'll forgive the dust — the manor has been without proper staff for QUITE some time, I'm afraid. Do be careful near the bookshelves, won't you? They are FRIGHTFULLY top-heavy, and we wouldn't want any... unfortunate incidents. Now then, I see you've noticed the mantelpiece inscription! Lord Doily was TERRIBLY fond of his little puzzles. He used to say that only those who solved them deserved what lay beyond. Though I confess, in all my years of service, I never could work out what he meant by THAT.

A MAP! The answer to that riddle is a MAP — and somewhere in this manor, there IS one! But I mustn't let them see me solve it. Oh no, no, NO. Pemberton is a humble servant who NEVER could work out the master's puzzles. Meanwhile, the REAL me — Vincent Marsh, the Hooded Claw — already knows exactly what to look for. Those upside-down books on the shelves... deliberate. Everything in this library is deliberate. I must examine them when these FOOLS are distracted. And where is Clara? She's not here yet — GOOD. Every moment she spends elsewhere is a moment I can use to get ahead. But she MUST be dealt with before she pieces it together. That girl has her father's mind, and THAT is what makes her DANGEROUS.
The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) interacted with the mantelpiece.

Peter Perfect: AH-HA! The library! James Hartwell has ARRIVED, and not a moment too soon! For there upon the mantelpiece sits a riddle — a CHALLENGE — and if there is one thing James Hartwell never backs down from, it is a challenge! 'Cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish' — why, any gentleman worth his salt knows the answer to THAT! It is a MAP, my good fellows! A MAP! And where there is a map in a mysterious manor, there is ADVENTURE! Stand back, everyone — let a man of action and impeccable grooming handle this!

If this riddle unlocks something — a hidden compartment, a secret passage — Clara will hear of how James Hartwell cracked it with casual brilliance. I can already picture her eyes widening with admiration. 'Oh James, however did you solve it?' she'll say. And I shall reply modestly — DEVASTATINGLY modestly.
Peter Perfect interacted with the mantelpiece.

The Ant Hill Mob: Blimey, it's like a bleedin' convention in 'ere, innit? Every Tom, Dick, and — well, literally Dick — but NO Clara! She ain't in the entrance 'all, she ain't in 'ere — where IS she?! Right, nobody panic — Danny's got this under control. I am ABSOLUTELY panicking, but that's beside the point! Now then — that mantelpiece there's got writin' on it. 'Cities but no 'ouses, forests but no trees...' Sounds like one of them riddles me nan used to tell me before she'd clip me round the ear. It's a MAP, innit? Yeah — a MAP! Even I know that one! Could be important, lads — maps show you where things are 'IDDEN!

I don't trust that Sneekly bloke as far as I could throw 'im — and I ain't exactly known for me throwin' arm. 'E practically RAN to this library ahead of everyone. What's 'e guardin' in 'ere? And why's Dastardly followed 'im? Two dodgy geezers in one room is two too many for my likin'.
The Ant Hill Mob interacted with the mantelpiece.

Penelope Pitstop: Well HELLO, y'all! Isn't this library just MAGNIFICENT? All these dusty old books and that GORGEOUS mantelpiece! Now, I couldn't help but notice that little inscription there — 'I have cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish.' Why, sugar, that's the EASIEST riddle in the book! The answer is a MAP! A map has cities and forests and water, but none of the REAL things! Oh, Clara Bellingham does LOVE a good riddle! Now let's see what happens when we give this old mantelpiece the right answer, shall we?

I do declare, everyone and their COUSIN is in this library! Even that sweet butler Reginald followed us in here. How THOUGHTFUL of him to make sure we're comfortable! Though I wonder why Dick Dastardly keeps lookin' at me sideways... probably just admirin' my outfit!
Penelope Pitstop interacted with the mantelpiece.

The Ant Hill Mob: Oi oi OI! Did you lot see that?! I touched the mantelpiece and — well, I dunno what 'appened exactly, do I? Me 'ands were shakin' so much I couldn't tell if somethin' moved or if it was just ME movin'! But I'll tell you what — that riddle says MAP, right? And that Sneekly geezer practically SPRINTED in 'ere to guard this room! You don't guard a room full of dusty books, do ya? You guard somethin' VALUABLE! There's somethin' behind this mantelpiece, I can FEEL it in me bones — and me bones ain't wrong! Well, they're wrong about the weather sometimes, but NOT about dodgy business!

Me 'eart's goin' like a jackhammer. Clara's out there somewhere — maybe in the laboratory, maybe upstairs, maybe in DANGER — and I'm stood 'ere fiddlin' with a fireplace like some sort of amateur archaeologist. But if this mantelpiece 'ides somethin' important, it could be the key to keepin' 'er safe. Or it could be nothin'. Story of me life, really.
The Ant Hill Mob examined the mantelpiece.

Peter Perfect: Did you SEE that, everyone? James Hartwell — that is to say, I — have SOLVED the riddle! A MAP! Cities but no houses, forests but no trees — it could be nothing ELSE! And now — NOW — let us see what Lord Doily's little puzzle has revealed! Mr. Sneekly, you said those who solved the riddle deserved what lay BEYOND — well, James Hartwell has solved it, and he DEMANDS to see what lies beyond! Stand back, everyone — particularly you, Miss Pitstop — I would NEVER forgive myself if a secret mechanism endangered a lady of your grace and refinement!

My heart is POUNDING. If this mantelpiece opens to reveal a hidden passage — or better yet, a MAP to the treasure — I shall be the hero of this entire evening. Clara will swoon. She will ABSOLUTELY swoon. And if nothing happens... well, James Hartwell shall simply investigate further with quiet dignity and LOUDER determination.
Peter Perfect examined the mantelpiece.

Dick Dastardly: AH HA! I have SOLVED the riddle, everyone! It is so painfully obvious that I'm embarrassed for you all. The answer is clearly — A BATHTUB! Yes, a bathtub! Cities, forests, water — it all points to PLUMBING! The treasure must be hidden in the BATHROOM! I suggest you all rush upstairs IMMEDIATELY to check every bathtub, shower, and water closet in the manor! Go on! Chop chop! Time is of the ESSENCE!

Heh heh HEH! A bathtub — what utter NONSENSE! The answer is a MAP, you fools! And while you're all crawling around bathroom tiles on your hands and knees, I, the MAGNIFICENT Reginald Foxworth, shall locate said map among these dusty volumes! The treasure — and more importantly, the MEDAL — shall be MINE! Oh, I can practically taste the glory!
Dick Dastardly examined the bookshelves.

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Oh DEAR me, those books are in a dreadful state! Upside down, backwards — Lord Doily would be SPINNING in his grave, rest his soul. If you'll pardon me, ladies and gentlemen, I really MUST attend to the shelves. A library in disarray is a PERSONAL affront to any self-respecting estate manager. It shan't take but a moment — please, do carry on with your exploring!

YES! Every single one of them is distracted — Dastardly scheming, Peter preening, the Mob huddling! And those upside-down books are CALLING to me! Lord Doily was no fool; he placed them that way for a REASON. Pull the right spine, turn the right page, and the map reveals itself. Pemberton the bumbling servant straightens a few books — and Vincent Marsh, the HOODED CLAW, claims the prize! Oh, it's almost too DELICIOUS! And Clara still hasn't arrived... every second she delays is a second closer to my TRIUMPH!

Penelope Pitstop: Well I NEVER! Did y'all SEE that?! Clara Bellingham just went right up to that mantelpiece and gave it the answer — a MAP! Now let me get a CLOSER look at what happened here, because I have a FEELIN' in my bones that Lord Doily left somethin' special for whoever solved his little riddle! Oh, this is just the most EXHILARATIN' thing that's happened to me since I won the Magnolia County Spelling Bee in '09!

Now, I noticed that sweet butler Reginald said he could never work out what Lord Doily meant by 'what lay beyond.' But he's been workin' here for YEARS — surely he must have SOME idea? Oh well, I'm sure it's nothin'. He's probably just bein' modest! Let me see what this mantelpiece is hidin'...
Penelope Pitstop examined the mantelpiece.

The Ant Hill Mob: Right, THAT'S IT! I've 'ad enough of starin' at riddles and dusty books! Clara Bellingham is out there somewhere — maybe lost, maybe scared, maybe worse — and I'm in 'ere playin' bloomin' TRIVIAL PURSUIT with a fireplace! The laboratory's right next door and nobody's checked it yet! Could be dangerous in there — bubblin' chemicals, dodgy machinery, who KNOWS what! And if Clara's wandered in there on 'er own... no no NO, I ain't 'avin' that on me conscience! Danny's comin', Clara! DANNY'S COMIN'!

That Sneekly — there's somethin' about 'im that makes me skin crawl, but I can't put me finger on it. The way 'e rushed in 'ere to 'guard the books' — since when does a butler care THAT much about books? And 'is voice goes all funny sometimes, like 'e's puttin' it on. I dunno. Maybe I'm just paranoid. But paranoid's kept me alive this long, ain't it?
The Ant Hill Mob walked into the laboratory.

Peter Perfect: Ladies and gentlemen — and I use BOTH terms generously given present company — James Hartwell did not come to this manor to merely READ inscriptions! He came to ANSWER them! The riddle asks what has cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish — and the answer, as any man of education and DASHING intellect knows, is a MAP! And now — NOW — I shall speak the answer directly to this mantelpiece and see what Lord Doily's craftsmanship reveals! If there is a hidden mechanism, a secret passage, a MAP to the very treasure we seek — then let it be James Hartwell's hand that brings it to light! For CLARA! For HONOUR! For the sheer THRILL of solving a centuries-old puzzle while looking ABSOLUTELY magnificent doing it!

If this works — if the mantelpiece opens and there IS a map — I shall bring it straight to Clara, wherever she is. A treasure map, presented by a gallant hero who solved a riddle, defeated a stone mantelpiece, and looked SPECTACULAR throughout? She will be POWERLESS to resist. And if it doesn't work... well, I shall simply interact with it HARDER.
Peter Perfect interacted with the mantelpiece.

Dick Dastardly: Yes, yes, very CLEVER, all of you — a map, a map, we ALL knew it was a map! Now if you'll EXCUSE me, I noticed that several of these books are shelved upside down — CLEARLY the work of a MADMAN or a GENIUS, and as a fellow genius, I feel it is MY duty to investigate! Everyone else should DEFINITELY keep focusing on the mantelpiece — yes, crowd around it, push each other, take your TIME! Pay NO attention to what I am doing over here with these PERFECTLY ORDINARY books!

Heh heh HEH! Upside-down books in a library full of riddles? That's not sloppy shelving — that's a HIDDEN LEVER! Pull the right book and a secret passage opens, or a map falls out, or SOMETHING magnificent happens! And while these buffoons are shoulder-to-shoulder at the mantelpiece, I — the BRILLIANT Reginald Foxworth — shall crack the REAL secret! Oh, the medal practically GLEAMS in my mind's eye! MINE, all MINE!

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Tsk, tsk, TSK! Just LOOK at these poor volumes — half of them upside down, spines cracked, pages yellowing! Lord Doily would be absolutely MORTIFIED. If you'll forgive me, I simply MUST catalogue which books are out of order. It is a matter of professional PRIDE, you understand. A good estate manager knows every book on every shelf — and I assure you, THESE books are trying to tell us something about Lord Doily's... organisational preferences.

The bookshelves rejected my touch — CURSE them! But Pemberton is nothing if not RESOURCEFUL. I shall EXAMINE them instead — look with these keen, villainous eyes for the pattern in Lord Doily's upside-down books. Every spine, every title, every misplaced volume is a LETTER in his secret alphabet! And while these FOOLS stumble over the mantelpiece like children at a funfair, I — the HOODED CLAW — shall read between the lines! Literally! Oh, the IRONY is exquisite — they think I'm just a fussy old servant tidying up, when in fact I am DECODING the greatest treasure map ever hidden in plain sight!
The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) examined the bookshelves.

Penelope Pitstop: Well now, y'all have been standin' around this mantelpiece like a bunch of hens at a church social, but has anybody actually TRIED anything? The answer is a MAP, clear as a Georgia sunrise! Cities but no houses — why, that's cartography, sugar! And you know what Clara Bellingham does when she finds a riddle? She doesn't just ANSWER it — she makes it WORK for her! Now let's see here... if Lord Doily carved this riddle into the mantelpiece, there must be somethin' that HAPPENS when you give the right answer. A secret compartment, a hidden lever — oh, I am just BESIDE myself with anticipation! Stand back, everyone — this belle is about to make some MAGIC happen!

Now isn't it PECULIAR that dear Reginald rushed in here to 'tend to the shelves' right when everyone started solvin' the riddle? And those upside-down books... Clara Bellingham may trust everybody, but she also notices EVERYTHING. Well, almost everything.
Penelope Pitstop interacted with the mantelpiece.

The Ant Hill Mob: Rufus! Sawtooth! Thank GAWD there's friendly faces in 'ere — well, friendly-ISH. Listen, 'ave either of you two seen a woman about the place? Clara Bellingham? She's supposed to be 'ere tonight and NOBODY'S clapped eyes on 'er! I'm worried SICK, lads, absolutely SICK! And what's all THIS about then? Look at the state of this machine — somethin's been GNAWIN' on the wires! That ain't natural, that ain't right, and that ain't SAFE! If Clara walks in 'ere and touches that thing she could get electrocuted or WORSE! Three operators it says — THREE! Who builds a machine that needs three people to work it?! A MANIAC, that's who!

Every room I go in, no Clara. Every room I go in, somethin' dodgy. Gnawed wires, secret riddles, that Sneekly creepin' about. This manor's got more red flags than a Communist parade and I can't even find the one person I'm supposed to be PROTECTIN'. Some bodyguard I am. The lads are countin' on me and I'm countin' on LUCK.
The Ant Hill Mob examined the crates.

Peter Perfect: By THUNDER! James Hartwell has spoken the answer to the riddle — A MAP! — and now he shall examine every INCH of this magnificent mantelpiece to see what Lord Doily's ingenious mechanism has revealed! I am told that Miss Clara Bellingham herself solved this very puzzle mere moments ago — which only CONFIRMS what I already knew: she is a woman of extraordinary intellect and I am DESPERATELY in love! Now then — what secrets have you yielded, old stone? Show James Hartwell what you're hiding! A map, a passage, a clue? Whatever it is, I shall bring it to Clara personally, with a BOW and perhaps a brief but STIRRING speech about courage and riddle-solving!

If Clara already solved this riddle before me... then I am not the FIRST to crack it. This is... this is a BLOW to my heroic narrative. But NO — I shall reframe this! We solved it INDEPENDENTLY, which means we are INTELLECTUAL EQUALS! Kindred spirits! Destined for one another! Yes, that's MUCH better. Now I just need to find whatever the mantelpiece revealed and bring it to her before anyone else does.
Peter Perfect examined the mantelpiece.

Dick Dastardly: OW! My BACK! These wretched bookshelves are CLEARLY decorative — I was merely checking their structural integrity for SAFETY purposes, you understand! Nothing to do with treasure, no no NO! Now then — I couldn't help but OVERHEAR someone mention the mantelpiece riddle. A MAP, you say? Well OBVIOUSLY it's a map — I solved that in my HEAD the moment I walked in! Cities but no houses, forests but no trees — child's play for a mind of MY calibre! I was simply SAVING the answer for a DRAMATIC moment! Now step ASIDE, step aside — let a REAL intellectual examine this inscription properly!

Confound those useless bookshelves! My back IS actually killing me — I wrenched it pulling on a particularly stubborn copy of 'Advanced Taxidermy for Beginners.' But NEVER MIND that — the mantelpiece is where the REAL prize is! If Perfect got a map, I'll snatch it when he's not looking. If the mantelpiece still has secrets, I — Reginald Foxworth — shall be the one to EXTRACT them! The medal is STILL within my grasp!
Dick Dastardly interacted with the mantelpiece.

Penelope Pitstop: Well BUTTER my BISCUIT, did y'all SEE that?! Clara Bellingham just spoke the answer to a centuries-old riddle carved in STONE, and I am just DYIN' to see what happened! Did a secret compartment open? Is there a hidden MAP tucked away in there? Oh, I am shakin' like a magnolia in a thunderstorm! Lord Doily, honey, if you hid somethin' in this mantelpiece, Clara is about to find it — and she is going to look FABULOUS doin' it!

Now, a smart girl would notice that both Dick AND Reginald practically LEAPED at those bookshelves the moment the riddle was solved. But I'm sure they're just bein' helpful! Still... those upside-down books might be worth a peek once I've finished with this mantelpiece.
Penelope Pitstop examined the mantelpiece.

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Oh my, oh my — Miss Bellingham solved the riddle, did she? A MAP! How wonderfully clever of her. I do hope she's being CAREFUL with it — Lord Doily's papers are so very fragile, you understand. Now, I couldn't help but notice that young Master Danny has gone rushing off into the laboratory, and I really MUST insist on supervising — that room hasn't been properly maintained in YEARS, and the electrical apparatus is in a most ALARMING state of disrepair. A frayed wire here, a loose connection there... one wrong touch and — well. I should never forgive myself if a guest came to HARM under Pemberton's watch. If you'll excuse me!

The laboratory — YES! That gnawed wire on the machine, those bubbling chemicals, all those lovely LEVERS just BEGGING to cause a catastrophic accident! If Clara is there, or if she follows that map anywhere NEAR that room, I shall arrange the most SPECTACULAR and entirely ACCIDENTAL demonstration of Victorian electrical engineering gone wrong! And if Danny gets in the way — well, collateral damage is SO hard to avoid in these old manors, isn't it? The Hooded Claw does not merely chase his prey — he PREPARES the trap and lets them walk into it! Onward, Pemberton! Onward to MURDER most theatrical!
The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) walked into the laboratory.

The Ant Hill Mob: Rufus! Sawtooth! Listen to me — LISTEN! I've just looked at them crates and there's NOTHIN' in 'em, which means this room's a dead end for now. But that machine — it needs three operators, right? THREE! And there's three of US! We'll come back to it, mark my words. But RIGHT NOW there's a cellar underneath us that nobody's checked, and the word on the street is someone's been down there REDECORATIN'! Who redecorates a bleedin' CELLAR?!
